reconcile.note: Gill answers that the disciples' sorrow arose from their confusion, not comprehension, so Matthew's sorrow and Mark's and Luke's incomprehension describe one bewildered reaction.

discrepancy.note: Strauss presses the dilemma: either the disciples' reported incomprehension is unhistorical exaggeration, or Jesus never made the plain disclosure Matthew implies.

quotes.text: we find the words of Mark (ix. 32) , But they understood not that saying … thus amplified in Luke: and it was hid from them, that they perceived it not
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), §112, on Mark 9:32 and Luke 9:45.

sides.verseText: But they didn't understand this saying. It was concealed from them, that they should not perceive it, and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.
